mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand offset by a construction rebound, resulting in flat S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: late-cycle consumer softening with housing recovery
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are significantly negative (< -1%) in more than 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for two consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below their 12-month moving averages by more than 0.5 percentage points signals a deflationary easing regime, which increases risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by at least 2% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a paradoxical labor market regime where job creation is offset by a broader labor force expansion, resulting in neutral S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: broad labor force expansion with stable employment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are significantly negative (< -0.5%) in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) below its 4-quarter moving average by more than 1% signals a broad-based demand contraction, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
